title: Engineering notation
common_pitfall: Do not add mantissas or forget the negative exponent.

title: Parallel resistors
problem: Find equivalent resistance of 120 Ω and 180 Ω in parallel. Answer in ohms.
common_pitfall: Put the full denominator in parentheses.

title: Parallel resistors
problem: Find equivalent resistance of 150 Ω and 300 Ω in parallel. Answer in ohms.
common_pitfall: A two-resistor parallel equivalent must be below the smaller resistor.

title: RC cutoff frequency
problem: For a first-order RC circuit with R=1000 Ω and C=0.1 μF, calculate fc=1/(2πRC) in hertz. Use at least 2 decimals.
common_pitfall: μF must be converted to F and π must not be omitted.

title: RC cutoff frequency
problem: For a first-order RC circuit with R=2000 Ω and C=0.22 μF, calculate fc=1/(2πRC) in hertz. Use at least 2 decimals.
common_pitfall: Using 0.22 F instead of 0.22 μF gives a millionfold error.

title: Power ratio in decibels
problem: Calculate the decibel gain for a linear POWER ratio Pout/Pin=100. Answer in dB.
common_pitfall: The factor is 10 for power ratios, not 20.

title: Power ratio in decibels
problem: Calculate the decibel gain for a linear POWER ratio Pout/Pin=50. Answer in dB, to two decimals.
common_pitfall: The 50 supplied is a linear ratio, not a dB value.

title: Ideal Nyquist sampling
problem: An ideal band-limited signal has highest frequency 7.5 kHz. Find the theoretical minimum sample rate in kHz.
independent_check: Half the sample rate is 7.5 kHz.
common_pitfall: Actual system design often needs margin above this theoretical limit.

title: Ideal Nyquist sampling
problem: An ideal band-limited signal has highest frequency 18 kHz. Find the theoretical minimum sample rate in kHz.
common_pitfall: Do not convert kHz into Hz without also converting the answer unit.

title: DC electric power
problem: Calculate P=VI for V=12 V and I=0.35 A. Answer in watts.
common_pitfall: Do not read 0.35 A as 35 A.

title: DC electric power
problem: Calculate P=VI for V=24 V and I=0.125 A. Answer in watts.
common_pitfall: Power P=VI assumes the stated voltage is across the current-carrying element.
